vectors.criterion: Two current bindings and candidate identity links share one asset and complete semantic revision 2; bindings retain canonical ID order and local object revision 1. No native qualification is asserted.

Revision 3 retires only source b and binding b, withdraws its candidate identity link and advances its publication cursor; all unrelated content and the historical snapshot remain unchanged. Retirement preserves tombstones without granting authority.

Against the coherent two-binding snapshot, upserting binding b at local revision 3 from revision 1 fails the publication successor rule with revision_conflict and retains the last known good snapshot. Grafting the later retired binding into the earlier current-source snapshot also fails the lifecycle reference rule after resealing. Object revisions are not semantic revision timestamps.
A resealed snapshot with binding b owned by another asset fails the Snapshot binding ownership rule, independently of digest validation.
Removing binding b while retaining its identity link fails the Snapshot identity binding reference rule. A binding is required by the retained reference, not by an invented minimum binding count.
Duplicating binding b in a resealed snapshot fails the existing ordered-unique binding identity rule.
